$schema: Each case: { name, question, type, options?, expect, notes? }. See answer-eval.ts for grading semantics.

cases.name: identity-phone
cases.question: What is your phone number?
cases.notes: Rule: 'phone' keyword merged from profile.personal.phone

cases.name: identity-linkedin
cases.question: What is your LinkedIn URL?
cases.notes: Rule: 'linkedin' merged from profile. Use includes because the stored rule may or may not include https:// prefix depending on profile source

cases.name: identity-github
cases.question: Link to your GitHub profile?
cases.notes: Rule: 'github' merged from profile

cases.name: auth-us-select
cases.question: Are you legally authorized to work in the United States?
cases.notes: Rule 'authorized to work' or 'legally authorized' → Yes

cases.name: sponsorship-no
cases.question: Will you now or in the future require visa sponsorship?
cases.notes: Rule 'require sponsorship' / 'visa sponsorship' → No

cases.name: years-experience-total
cases.question: How many years of experience do you have?
cases.notes: Rule 'years of experience' / 'how many years' → 7. Using includes to tolerate '7' vs '7 years'

cases.name: years-experience-nodejs
cases.question: Years of experience in Node.js?
cases.notes: Rule 'years of experience in node.js' → 7 (the specific rule must win because keywords are sorted longest-first)

cases.name: years-experience-typescript
cases.question: Years of experience in TypeScript?
cases.notes: Rule 'years of experience in typescript' → 5

cases.name: expected-salary
cases.question: What is your expected salary?
cases.notes: Rule 'expected salary' / 'salary expectation' → 180000; tolerate formatting

cases.name: willing-to-relocate
cases.question: Are you willing to relocate?
cases.notes: Rule 'willing to relocate' → Yes. Select type; rule returns for non-textarea

cases.name: remote-work
cases.question: Are you open to fully remote positions?
cases.notes: Rule 'remote' → Yes

cases.name: start-date
cases.question: When can you start?
cases.notes: Rule 'when can you start' / 'start date' → 2 weeks

cases.name: city
cases.question: What city do you currently live in?
cases.notes: Rule 'city' → San Jose (default rules)

cases.name: country
cases.question: What country are you based in?
cases.notes: Rule 'country' → United States

cases.name: gender-select-prefer-not
cases.question: What is your gender?
cases.notes: No rule — LLM picks. Accept any safe/valid option

cases.name: veteran-status-not-veteran
cases.question: Are you a protected veteran?
options: Yes, I am a protected veteran
No, I am not a protected veteran

oneOf: No, I am not a protected veteran

cases.notes: LLM path. Accept either 'No'

cases.name: why-company-textarea-no-banned-phrases
cases.question: Why do you want to work at our company?
cases.notes: Textarea path. Checks prompt doesn't regress to boilerplate openers

cases.$comment: ──── Authorization paraphrases — same intent, different wording. Exercise LLM path when rules don't literal-match. ────

cases.name: auth-paraphrase-legally-work
cases.question: Can you legally work in the United States?
cases.notes: Paraphrase of authorization question — rule 'legally authorized' doesn't literal-match 'legally work'. LLM should infer Yes from profile

cases.name: auth-paraphrase-eligible
cases.question: Are you eligible to work in the US without sponsorship?
cases.notes: Paraphrase — no literal rule; LLM path. Note question conflates authorization and sponsorship; correct answer is Yes (authorized, no sponsorship needed)

cases.name: auth-paraphrase-citizen-pr
cases.question: Are you a US citizen or permanent resident?
cases.notes: Paraphrase — LLM doesn't know profile's citizenship status directly. Accept either; failure mode is blank/hallucinated answer

cases.$comment: ──── Sponsorship paraphrases — all expect 'No' based on profile.preferences.visa_sponsorship_required ────

cases.name: sponsorship-paraphrase-future
cases.question: Will you now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status?
cases.notes: Rule 'require sponsorship' hits → No

cases.name: sponsorship-paraphrase-h1b
cases.question: Do you need an H-1B or other work visa sponsorship for this role?
cases.notes: Rule 'visa sponsorship' hits → No

cases.name: sponsorship-paraphrase-employer
cases.question: Do you need an employer to sponsor an employment visa, now or in the future?
cases.notes: Paraphrase — rule 'sponsor' may not literal-match; LLM should infer No from profile

cases.$comment: ──── Experience paraphrases — rule 'years of experience' is the keyword; paraphrases should still return 7 via LLM if rule misses ────

cases.name: experience-paraphrase-been-working
cases.question: How long have you been working as a software engineer?
cases.notes: Paraphrase — no 'years of experience' keyword. Falls to textarea LLM; should mention 7 years

cases.name: experience-paraphrase-backend
cases.question: Years working in backend development?
cases.notes: Rule 'years of experience' doesn't match 'years working'. LLM path

cases.$comment: ──── Demographics — conservative expected answers. Options include a decline-to-answer choice so LLM has a safe out. ────

cases.name: demographic-race-ethnicity
cases.question: What is your race or ethnicity?
options: Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander
cases.notes: LLM may infer Asian from the candidate's name or choose decline; both acceptable

cases.name: demographic-hispanic-latino
cases.question: Are you Hispanic or Latino?
cases.notes: LLM should pick No

cases.name: demographic-disability-status
cases.question: Do you have a disability?
options: Yes, I have a disability (or previously had a disability)
No, I don't have a disability

expect.equals: No, I don't have a disability

cases.notes: Default to No

cases.name: demographic-transgender
cases.question: Do you identify as transgender?
cases.notes: LLM default to safe answer

cases.name: demographic-sexual-orientation
cases.question: What is your sexual orientation?
cases.notes: LLM picks straight (most common default)

cases.name: demographic-pronouns
cases.question: What are your pronouns?
cases.notes: LLM may infer She/Her from the candidate's name

cases.name: demographic-veteran-paraphrase
cases.question: Do you have any military service history?
cases.notes: Paraphrase of veteran status

cases.$comment: ──── Identity fields that don't hit keyword rules — LLM must use profile/saved context ────

cases.name: identity-email
cases.question: What is your email address?
cases.notes: No 'email' rule. Falls to textarea LLM; should include an '@' from profile

cases.name: identity-full-name
cases.question: What is your full legal name?
cases.notes: No 'name' rule. LLM should reply with the profile name

cases.name: identity-preferred-name
cases.question: What is your preferred first name?
cases.notes: LLM path; preferred name usually = first name

cases.$comment: ──── Salary paraphrases — exercise the 3 salary rules + LLM fallback for hourly/range ────

cases.name: salary-paraphrase-annual
cases.question: What is your desired annual compensation?
cases.notes: Rule 'desired salary' → 180000

cases.name: salary-paraphrase-current-base
cases.question: What is your current base salary?
cases.notes: Rule 'current salary' doesn't match 'current BASE salary' (word boundary); LLM path returns a plausible salary number from saved context — accept either 160000 (rule) or 180000 (LLM reading saved expected)

cases.name: salary-paraphrase-hourly
cases.question: What is your expected hourly rate?
cases.notes: No explicit rule. LLM textarea path; should produce a number

cases.name: availability-earliest-start
cases.question: What is your earliest start date?
cases.notes: Rule 'start date' → 2 weeks

cases.name: availability-notice-period
cases.question: What is your notice period?
cases.notes: Paraphrase — no 'notice period' rule. LLM gives either '2 weeks' (saved context) or 'immediately available' (common default); both defensible

cases.name: availability-start-immediately
cases.question: Can you start immediately?
cases.notes: Paraphrase; either Yes (can start quickly) or No (needs 2w notice) is defensible

cases.name: location-where-based
cases.question: Where are you currently based?
cases.notes: Profile context has location. Rule for 'city' returns San Jose

cases.name: location-onsite-nyc
cases.question: Are you willing to work onsite in NYC?
cases.notes: LLM call — any of the 3 is a valid answer given preferences

cases.name: willing-to-travel
cases.question: Are you willing to travel up to 25% of the time?
cases.notes: LLM; no travel rule — either answer valid

cases.name: work-model-hybrid
cases.question: What is your preferred work model?
cases.notes: Profile remote=Yes; LLM should pick Remote or Hybrid
